intro_html: Gyro flavor without the giant vertical rotisserie is exactly what a slow cooker is for. This bowl packs 65 grams of protein for about $4.10 (at everyday cost), topped with a cool yogurt sauce that plays off the savory chicken. Fourteen servings means one afternoon of prep feeds you well past the week.
cost_closing_html: About $4.10 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
portion_html: Each serving carries 65 grams of protein and 573 calories, lean and filling in equal measure.
upsell_html: All the flavor of the food-truck favorite, none of the food-truck markup. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
shop_smart: Onions are one of the cheapest ways to build flavor, so keep a bag on the counter and lean on them.
That same tub of Greek yogurt sauces both the gyro and the shawarma bowls, so buy one tub and cover two recipes.
Skip the specialty gyro seasoning and mix oregano, garlic powder, and a little onion powder from your own rack.
make_it: Add the chicken, olive oil, sliced onion, and garlic to the slow cooker and stir to combine.
Cover and cook on low for 6 to 7 hours until the chicken is tender and shreddable.
Stir the Greek yogurt and lime juice together for a quick tzatziki-style sauce and chill it.
Steam or roast the broccoli florets to round out the bowl.
Shred the chicken over white rice with the broccoli, then finish with the yogurt sauce.
